card.summary: The Digital Commodity Intermediaries Act establishes a regulatory framework for digital commodities under the jurisdiction of the Commodity Futures Trading Commission (CFTC). It sets up registration, operational, and reporting requirements for digital commodity exchanges, brokers, and dealers, and creates protections for software developers and customer asset segregation.

summary: The Digital Commodity Intermediaries Act establishes a regulatory framework for digital commodities under the Commodity Futures Trading Commission. It requires digital commodity exchanges, brokers, and dealers to register with the agency, imposes customer protection and asset segregation rules, and outlines requirements for qualified digital asset custodians.

affected_groups.effect: Must register with the Commodity Futures Trading Commission, comply with new operational, reporting, and capital requirements, and pay regulatory fees.
affected_groups.group: Digital commodity exchanges, brokers, and dealers

affected_groups.effect: Receive enhanced asset segregation, disclosure standards, and access to a new Digital Commodity Retail Advocate for assistance with disputes.
Exempted from standard broker-dealer regulations when performing core protocol, node operation, or software development tasks on blockchains.

key_provisions: Grants the Commodity Futures Trading Commission exclusive jurisdiction over digital commodity spot and cash transactions offered or executed by registered entities.
Requires digital commodity exchanges, brokers, and dealers to register with the Commodity Futures Trading Commission and establishes an expedited registration process.
Mandates that registered entities hold customer digital assets in qualified digital asset custodians and keep them strictly segregated from company funds.
Establishes protections for software developers, exempting activities such as code writing, running nodes, or providing user interfaces from regulation under the Act.
Creates the Office of the Digital Commodity Retail Advocate within the Commodity Futures Trading Commission to assist retail participants and propose regulatory changes.
Authorizes the collection of fees from registered entities to fund the implementation and oversight activities of the Commodity Futures Trading Commission.
missing_information: Specific numerical fee amounts or rates that the Commodity Futures Trading Commission will assess on registered entities.
Exact definitions of de minimis trading or transaction volumes that would exempt certain small operators from registration requirements.
summary_detail.plain_summary: The Digital Commodity Intermediaries Act establishes a regulatory framework for digital commodities under the Commodity Futures Trading Commission. It requires digital commodity exchanges, brokers, and dealers to register with the agency, imposes customer protection and asset segregation rules, and outlines requirements for qualified digital asset custodians.
summary_detail.significance: This bill significantly reshapes federal oversight of cryptocurrency and digital assets by bringing spot markets and intermediaries under the direct regulatory authority of the Commodity Futures Trading Commission.
